messages:
maria: heads-up — i'm prepping a cross-account MRK failover test between acct-A (primary) and acct-B (replica). quick question: if we rotate the primary in acct-A, will existing ciphertexts encrypted under the pre-rotation material still decrypt via the replica in acct-B during the rotation window?

sanjay: short: good call to test. my recollection is that MRKs are meant to be interoperable (primary/replica can decrypt each other's ciphertexts) but rotation/replication timing can introduce weirdness. we should not assume instant replication.

ellie: +1. also watch cross-account grants/policy — replicas in another account need explicit key policy or grants to allow Decrypt for the role assuming into acct-B. worth validating both key policy and IAM principal permissions.

maria: thanks. plan: 1) create small test file, 2) encrypt with primary (acct-A), 3) verify decrypt in acct-A, 4) verify decrypt in acct-B via assumed role, 5) rotate primary, 6) re-run decrypts from both sides.

ops-oncall-bot: noting potential impact: if decrypt fails during rotation for production traffic, fallback should hit secondary model/service that uses a different KMS key. please avoid running on prod keys. :warning:

maria: absolutely not touching prod. test keys only. anyone have an AWS CLI snippet for cross-account decrypt via STS assume-role?

sanjay: here's a quick flow i used:
```bash
# assume role in acct-B
creds=$(aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_B:role/RedwoodKMSCrossAccountTest --role-session-name mrk-test)
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo $creds | jq -r .Credentials.AccessKeyId)
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(echo $creds | jq -r .Credentials.SecretAccessKey)
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(echo $creds | jq -r .Credentials.SessionToken)
# try decrypt with replica key ARN
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://payload.enc --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:ACCOUNT_B:key/REPLICA_KEY_ID --output text --query Plaintext | base64 --decode > decrypted.bin
```

ellie: good. also add a CloudTrail filter on KMS Decrypt events so we can see which key/region/account handled the decrypt call. that will prove where the decrypt actually executed.

maria: noted. one more Q: how does envelope encryption change behavior? if we use a data key generated by acct-A primary and then rotate primary, will the data key ciphertext still be decryptable by acct-B replica?

sanjay: conceptually the data key ciphertext is just KMS-encrypted blob. if the replica has the same key material (and AWS treats MRK as same logical key) it should be able to decrypt. but implementation details: if replication is async, there could be a window where the replica hasn't received the new material after rotation and might still decrypt older ciphertexts fine; rotation creates new key material for future generates. edge cases exist if you mix key ARNs vs multi-region key IDs. test to be safe.

maria: ok will log results. i'll also try rotating the replica (manual rotation) to see if behavior differs.

kms-bot: audit: created test MRK replica arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:ACCOUNT_B:key/REPLICA_KEY_ID by maria at 2026-03-20T15:41:07Z

ellie: one operational note — grants can be faster to propagate than key policy changes. for ephemeral tests, create a grant to allow the cross-account role Decrypt/GenerateDataKey permissions so you don't have to update key policy mid-test.

maria: good tip, i'll use a short-lived grant and then revoke. i'll post results + CloudTrail snippets here after the run. :white_check_mark:
